images.title: Saplings in groups of four
images.purpose: Show that 16 watered saplings out of 20 fill 4 of 5 equal groups of 4, so 16/20 can be written with smaller numbers as 4/5.
images.composition: One long row of saplings across the middle, split into five boxed groups with small gaps, and one result line centred below.
images.exact_structure: One row of 20 identical simple sapling icons (a short stem with two leaves), evenly spaced. Thin grey #6B7280 rounded boxes split the row into 5 groups of exactly 4 saplings each. The 16 saplings in the left 4 groups are filled teal #0072B2 (watered); the 4 saplings in the fifth group are plain outlines only. One fraction above the row, a short caption under the boxes, and one reddish purple #CC79A7 result line centred below. No soil, sky or people. Exactly 20 saplings, 5 boxes, 16 teal.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
groups that do not hold exactly 4 saplings, or the fraction 8/10 anywhere
images.takeaway: 16/20 in lowest terms is 4/5, because 4 is a common factor of 16 and 20.
images.description: A row of 20 saplings boxed into 5 groups of 4; the 16 in the first 4 groups are teal, showing 16/20 = 4/5.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the boxes and the teal boxes, and say why 16/20 is the same as 4/5.

image_decisions.why: Grouping the row by the common factor 4 makes lowest terms visible; one image of grouped saplings carries it.
